text:
Thursday was Jesper Bratt in miniature. The Devils blew a three-goal lead to St. Louis in the third, Dougie Hamilton sprang him on a breakaway in overtime, and Bratt finished it for a 5-4 win and a sixth straight home victory.

That goal was only his third of the season, and it's the number we'd ignore. Bratt has generated 4.71 expected goals (the quality of his chances), so he's about 1.7 short, shooting 8.8% against a typical range of 10 to 15 for him. The rest of his game is outstanding. New Jersey takes 66% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, ten points better than without him, which is about as dominant as a winger gets. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 98th percentile for driving play last season, against the other team's best.

He's a passer first (Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 94th percentile for primary shot assists), and the 12 assists show it. The goals should follow. Our range has him between 14 and 26 for the season, with 67 points the middle.
headline: Bratt's chances are better than his goal total
